column1: # Keyword groupings of GO terms, mirroring the KEGG BRITE categories.
# THESE ARE NOT AN ONTOLOGY. GO has no equivalent of KEGG's BRITE categories, so
# each group here is a regular expression matched against the GO term NAME. That
# is a text search, not a graph traversal: it will pull in terms that merely
# share a word and miss terms that describe the same biology in other words.
# Treat a panel as "GO terms whose names mention X", never as "everything GO
# knows about X". The plot subtitle says so too.
# Categories overlap by design - GOBP_NEURON_DIFFERENTIATION matches both
# nervous_system and development_and_regeneration - and a term may appear in
# several panels.
# Columns: slug <TAB> label <TAB> include <TAB> exclude
#   include  case-insensitive regex; a term is in the group if it matches
#   exclude  case-insensitive regex; matching terms are dropped again (may be
#            empty, written as "-")
